newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf Air needs urgent cash to service debts - paper.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air needs urgent cash to service debts - paper.

text.p: Gulf Air needs urgent cash to finance its estimated $1 billion in debts, the London-based Arabic newspaper Ashraq al-Awsat said on Sunday.
Quoting unnamed Gulf sources, the daily said Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) had "voiced their desire to pump more cash which the company needs urgently".
Gulf Air officials were not available for immediate comment.
The Bahrain-based airline is jointly owned by the governments of Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi emirate in the UAE.
It plans to lease more aircraft and cut unprofitable routes to help it return to profit after a $159 million loss in 1995.
The newspaper said Qatar and Oman were unlikely to pump more cash into the company to help pay its debts.
"UAE and Bahrain will demand that they buy the Qatari and Omani stakes in return for pumping liquidity into Gulf Air," the daily quoted the sources as saying.

The newspaper said Bahrain's Finance and National Economy Minister Ibrahim Abdel-Karim, accompanied by civil aviation officials, flew to Abu Dhabi on Saturday to review ways of servicing Gulf Air's debts. It gave no further details.
